result.title: Name a workflow once and reuse it
result.problem: A WorkflowProfile exists only as the bundled spec-ledger/default or as a custom profile embedded in one workstream snapshot, so there is nothing to select. Reuse is manual JSON export/import and there is no repo default. Portability is blocked by two per-workstream couplings: resolveWorkflow validates output.criterionIds against criterionIds(ws), which is positional per workstream, and validateOrder derives required stages from the target workstream's policy. profile.source is a closed default|custom union that roleApplicable and workflowOptions branch on, so a third source would silently change stage gating.
result.objective: Save a workflow under a name, pick which one is normal, and choose it for a spec instead of rebuilding the steps every time.
outOfScope: Different normal workflows per feature or per person
Sharing profiles between repositories or any registry
Migrating workflows already embedded in existing snapshots
rabbitHoles: Migrating existing embedded custom snapshots - the library is additive and old snapshots stay readable
Letting a library edit mutate a running spec as a side effect
Moving /workflows without updating the navigation test inside both b-sl-029 and b-sl-030 while SL-029 and SL-030 stay true
Re-implementing workflow validation rules inside packages/ui
Reusing editable() to save a profile without stripping the source spec's criterionIds - that reintroduces the portability bug
Sealing before SL-032/SL-033/SL-034 are promoted: acceptanceClaimIds is inside sealPayload, so a later fix drifts the seal digest

suggestedSlices.title: Save one workflow and use it on another spec
acceptance: Saving the workflow a spec is using, then adopting it by name on a second spec, produces a working workflow there without retyping steps, and records the saved workflow's id and version.
Saving a workflow is create-only: an id that already exists is refused and nothing is overwritten.
Requirement coverage is attached from the adopting spec, so a workflow saved from a spec with different acceptance criteria still applies cleanly.
Adopting a workflow that lacks a review stage the target spec requires is refused naming the missing stage, and nothing is stored.
Adopting a workflow whose skill file is missing, unreadable, outside the checkout or oversized is refused naming the path, and nothing is stored.
After editing or deleting the saved workflow, the adopting spec's stage statuses and evidence currency are unchanged.
A stage the spec's policy does not require stays applicable when the workflow marks it required, and adopting a saved copy of the bundled workflow gives the same stage statuses as adopting nothing.
suggestedSlices.notes: Stage applicability becomes stage.required ?? policy(role); profile.source stops feeding roleApplicable and becomes provenance only. packages/ledger/src/workflows/workflow.break.test.ts:372 (bound to required claim SL-024) changes with SL-024's statement intact. N-3: saving strips output.criterionIds at the editable() boundary; adoption attaches the adopting spec's criterionIds to every implementation-report and check-results output by kind, mirroring defaultStages, and never overwrites criteria an author wrote by hand.

suggestedSlices.title: Manage the saved workflows
acceptance: The list shows every saved workflow and marks which ones a chosen spec can use, and why the others cannot.
Two workflows cannot share an id; renaming changes title only and leaves adopted provenance intact.
Editing, deleting or changing the default requires the caller's expected version and is refused as a conflict when it has moved, changing nothing.
Deleting an adopted workflow is allowed and leaves those specs running, still showing its name marked deleted; deleting the default falls back to the bundled workflow.
Terminal and agent tools behave identically, and the local UI route refuses malformed, oversized and cross-site requests.
Every library change is recorded in the operations trail with its actor and reason.
suggestedSlices.notes: Default pointer lives in the workflows store, not schemas/ledger-root.json, which is additionalProperties:false. Reserve the pointer path so a profile whose id is 'default' cannot collide with it. N-5: .spec-ledger/** is in DEFAULT_ALIGN_IGNORE and excluded from sourceFingerprint, so align check will not surface library edits.

suggestedSlices.title: Choose a workflow where the work is
acceptance: A spec's workflow is readable and switchable beside its evidence and changes without a separate page, and switching records the reason preserveWorkflow already requires.
Defining a workflow is reachable only from the library screen, and switching a spec's workflow never requires restating its steps.
The editor shows stages and steps in run order with required results, rejects exactly what the engine rejects, and never offers a shape the engine cannot run.
A spec shows the name and version of the saved workflow it adopted, and marks it deleted when that workflow is gone.
suggestedSlices.notes: Editor guard rails come from the client's exported validation or preview round-trip, never a second copy of the rules in packages/ui. N-9: the route change touches packages/ui/lib/navigation.test.mjs:27, which is inside BOTH b-sl-029 and b-sl-030; the rewritten test must assert the new in-page workflow join and that /workflows/<W-id> no longer resolves. N-7: packages/ui/components/workflow-view.tsx:199,224 render a two-value default|custom badge.

residualRisks: Library edits live under .spec-ledger/, which align check ignores and the source fingerprint excludes, so they never appear in turn path coverage.
trust.requiredEvidence is advisory; no code enforces the e2e requirement.
